- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward moves in history; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.5% from first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not just magnitude.
